title: Restriction and regrouping of an unconditionally summable family
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative absolute value $|\cdot|:K\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$, complete for the metric $d(a,b)=|a-b|$. Let $I,J$ be arbitrary sets, and let $u:I\to K$ be summable, meaning that its sums over finite subsets converge, with sum $U$. For every subset $B\subset I$, the restricted family $(u_i)_{i\in B}$ is summable. For every map $p:I\to J$, put $v_j=\sum_{i\in p^{-1}(j)}u_i$. Then $(v_j)_{j\in J}$ is summable with sum $U$: $$\sum_{j\in J}\left(\sum_{i\in p^{-1}(j)}u_i\right)=\sum_{i\in I}u_i.$$ Empty fibers have sum zero; no countability, surjectivity, or finiteness assumption on the fibers is required. The absolute value need not be nonarchimedean.
